newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria buys 75,000 T wheat, probably French-trade.
newsitem.headline: Algeria buys 75,000 T wheat, probably French-trade.

text.p: Algeria on Wednesday bought 75,000 tonnes of European Union wheat for April/May shipment at around $180 per tonne, a price that equates to $160 or $161 per tonne fob France, grain traders said.
One trader said the wheat would be of European Union origin, while another senior trader said it was almost certain to come from France.
Traders said wheat export values were firm in France late on Wednesday with April French paper wheat bid around $164 a tonne.

The decision to buy French wheat came despite reports of friction between Paris and Algiers over remarks last week by France's prime minister, a row that apparently spilled over into Algeria's grain purchasing practices.
Traders said in the past 10 days that Algeria had unusually decided not to invite offers to supply wheat from the domestic offices of French companies at two successive import tenders.
It did however seem willing to buy French wheat from other companies or the foreign offices of French firms, they said.
The company reported to have sold the wheat on Wednesday does not have its headquarters in France.

Algeria's official press agency last week accused French Prime Minister Alain Juppe of interfering in its affairs after he called for a "true democratic conscience" to be established in France's violence-racked former colony.
